name: Congenital Pulmonary Vein Atresia

criteria.description: Absence or atresia of one or more pulmonary veins confirmed by imaging
Evidence of pulmonary venous congestion or pulmonary edema on imaging
Clinical signs of respiratory distress or recurrent pulmonary infections in infancy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent pulmonary vein(s) on imaging plus clinical or radiological evidence of pulmonary venous congestion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging modalities such as echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI.

pathognomonic.notes: Confirmed by imaging; hallmark of the disease
searchTerms: missing pulmonary vein on one side

pathognomonic.symptomName: Recurrent pulmonary infections localized to affected lung
searchTerms: frequent lung infections in one area
worsening shortness of breath with activity
failure to gain weight as baby

laboratory: Non-specific inflammatory markers may be elevated during infections
Arterial blood gas may show hypoxemia
imaging: Absent or atretic pulmonary vein on echocardiography, CT angiography, or MRI
Pulmonary venous congestion and edema on chest X-ray
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; sporadic cases reported
other: Bronchoscopy may reveal bronchial varices or congestion
Cardiac catheterization can confirm pulmonary venous obstruction and measure pulmonary pressures

distinguishingFeatures: All pulmonary veins drain anomalously to systemic veins or right atrium
Usually presents with cyanosis and heart failure in newborns
Narrowing rather than complete atresia of pulmonary veins
Progressive obstruction often post-surgical or idiopathic

redFlags: Severe respiratory distress in neonate or infant
Signs of pulmonary hypertension or right heart failure
references: Garg et al., Congenital Pulmonary Vein Atresia: Clinical and Imaging Features, Pediatric Cardiology, 2018
Orphanet Report on Congenital Pulmonary Vein Atresia, 2023
Mullins et al., Pulmonary Vein Atresia and Stenosis, Circulation, 2015
